name: Beehive Eats: Utah Restaurants
subtitle: Pastrami Burgers & Red Rock
description:
Utah's restaurants, from a pastrami burger with fry sauce to dinner in Torrey after Capitol Reef.

Beehive Eats is a free guide to eating in Utah: 15 Salt Lake classics, 21 red rock country stops, 15 Park City and canyon-town tables, 5 pastrami burger stands, 4 Pacific Islander kitchens and 4 pie stops we checked by hand, plus 6,168 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 199 towns, from Salt Lake City and Ogden to Moab and St. George. No account, no ads.

UTAH GUIDES
• Salt Lake Classics: the institutions, from Ruth's Diner to Red Iguana.
• Red Rock Country: stops near the national parks, Moab to Boulder.
• Pastrami Burgers & Fry Sauce: the Utah way.
• Hawaiian & Pacific Islander: Hawaiian, Tongan and Samoan plates and poke.
• Ski Towns: Park City's Main Street and the canyon towns.
• Pie Stops: on the scenic byways.
• MICHELIN & James Beard: the MICHELIN Guide's Utah selection and James Beard honorees (20 places).

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "pastrami burger", "torrey", "pie zion".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source or an official tourism listing. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule tested in the states that publish official restaurant lists; Utah publishes none. Utah's 13 health departments post reports only in their own searches, so each place links the list of health departments. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Beehive Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of Utah or any Utah health department), or with the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation. MICHELIN and the MICHELIN Guide are trademarks of Michelin. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Beehive Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Utah (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: Salt Lake classics, red rock country stops near the national parks, pastrami burgers, Pacific Islander plates, Park City's Main Street and pie stops, 64 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus 20 MICHELIN Guide and James Beard honorees. It also lists 6,168 restaurants, cafés and bars in 199 towns from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Salt Lake Classics (or Red Rock Country, Pastrami Burgers & Fry Sauce, Hawaiian & Pacific Islander, Ski Towns, Pie Stops, MICHELIN & James Beard, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, a link opens the list of Utah's local health departments in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("pastrami burger", "torrey", "pie zion").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Utah (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Utah, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Beehive Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Beehive Eats: Utah Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Beehive Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); MICHELIN Guide and James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites, local news and official tourism listings.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/utah-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Utah; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. The app shows no inspection results and computes no grades. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation.
